newsitem.title: PERU: Peru investigates cocaine found at U.N. mission.
newsitem.headline: Peru investigates cocaine found at U.N. mission.

text.p: Peruvian police were investigating drug smugglers who used a diplomatic bag to send two pounds (900 grams) of cocaine to the Peruvian mission at the United Nations, the Foreign Ministry said on Monday.

Peruvian diplomats at the United Nations found a package containing suspicious white powder, later identified by police tests as cocaine, addressed to a Peruvian civil servant in New York, from an ex-employee of the Peruvian Foreign Ministry.
Peru's acting Foreign Minister Jorge Gonzalez Izquierdo told a news conference: "Peruvian authorities will give all necessary support to find and punish those responsible."
His ministry said U.S. drug authorities had been informed.

The government of Peru has been embarrassed by drug scandals last year including accusations by a captured drug trafficker that President Alberto Fujimori's top security adviser gave protection to drug smugglers.
Also last year, bags of cocaine were discovered on two Peruvian Navy ships and on an Air Force plane. Peru is the world's largest producer of coca leaves, the raw material for cocaine.
